2027 Ducati Desmo450 EDX Gets New Six-Speed Gearbox and Retuned Suspension
13 photos
Photo: Ducati
Shortly after it presented to the world the first Desmo250 EDX motorcycle in its enduro and cross-country offering, Italian bike maker Ducati saw fit to present the updated version of the older 450 EDX as well. And there's quite a bit to be excited about.
Building on the platform that came to light for the first time at the end of last year, the machine brings to the enduro-cross table a new six-speed transmission, that replaces the previous five-speed one, along with updated final-drive gearing (13/50), and a retuned Showa suspension system, tailored specifically developed for cross-country riding.
The two-wheeler continues to be based on the Desmo450 MX platform that marked the bike maker's entry in this segment in the spring of 2025, and that means it is still animated by a 449.6cc Desmodromic single-cylinder engine that delivers 64 horsepower at 9,400 rpm and 39 lb-ft of torque at 7,500 rpm.
The engine draws its energy from a new, transparent tank that can hold 2.2 gallons (8.3 liters) of fuel. It also benefits from revised starter gear tolerances, an updated water-pump seal, and a reinforced exhaust mounting point.
I mentioned earlier the suspension system tailored for cross-country activities. That was achieved by Ducati engineers through the fitting of a fully adjustable 49 mm Showa inverted closed-cartridge fork with 310 mm (12.2 inches) of travel at the front, and a fully adjustable Showa monoshock that delivers 301 mm of wheel travel at the rear.
Speaking of wheels, these are fitted with Takasago Excel aluminum rims and continue to be sized 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear. They are both shod in Pirelli Scorpion XC Mid-Soft tires to be able to handle all kinds of terrain.
The Italians throw the 2027 Desmo450 EDX onto the market complete with a lot of standard fittings, including handguards, a skid plate, and a side stand. There are a few extras that have been thrown into the mix specifically for the 2027 model year, more specifically the updated shift and rear-brake pedal tips, revised engine mounting brackets, and a reinforced chain-guide support.
The upgraded motorcycle tips the scales at 237 pounds (108 kg) and will be dressed in a revised graphics package. All the changes, says Ducati, are meant to make the Desmo450 EDX even better than it already is at taking on both tricky sections and wide-open stretches.
We're told the new bike will become available at American dealers starting early next month. It will carry a starting price of $12,495, and, just like before, it will be eligible for the Ducati Race Rewards program.
That's the Italian manufacturer's off-road racing contingency program for the United States, through which Ducati supports privateer racers competing at approved events across the country.
